newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Publico surges on talk it made acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Publico surges on talk it made acquisition.

text.p: Shares in South African specialist publishing group, Publico Ltd, powered to fresh highs on Wednesday on rumours the firm had acquired another business, Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealers said.
By 1240 GMT Publico shares were up 85 cents or 23.6 percent at 445 cents. Shares earlier touched a day high of 470, well ahead of their best level this year of 390 cents touched in January.
"There are very strong rumours in the market that a deal was signed last night," said a dealer who asked not to be identified but who had been trading Publico shares.
Publico management could not immediately be reached for comment.
The firm, together with its holding company, Publico Holdings Ltd (Pubhold) on May 23 renewed an earlier cautionary notice advising shareholders that the two companies were in unspecified talks.
Asked what type of acquisition Publico could have made, another dealer said: "They are in publishing and its probably in that area."
Dealers said the share stood to gain considerable upside potential from the possible deal.
"The feeling is that it could take the shares up to eight or nine rand," one said.

Volumes were brisk with over 306,000 shares trading in Publico which is 75 percent owned by Pubhold. Pubhold shares jumped in tandem gaining a massive 52.7 percent to 550 cents after 17,600 shares had traded.
In the year to end-February Publico reported a slide in headline earnings to 14.6 cents a share compared with 26.1 a year ago. The dividend was halved to three cents from six before.
